supplementary_figure_S13_motivating_sett.note: Independent transcription of supplementary page 34 (a raster figure without a text layer, read at 160, 300 and 600 dpi) and of main Tables 1 and 2 (pp. 10-11). Panels a and b are illustrations and carry structural targets only: panel letters, titles, every setting name and description, the frozen-backbone and adapter box labels (theta, H_ell and A_ell in plain-text notation), the panel-b family titles, axis labels, the 0/L depth ticks and all three annotations, and, from the caption ('a common risk-minimizing transport admits one open-loop schedule'; 'input-dependent minima preclude a common optimum'), whether each family shares a risk minimizer. The number, shape and placement of the stylized curves (five per family in print), the dashed best-fixed-depth line, the minimum dots, the padlock pictogram and the box connector are drawing choices, not targets; no stylized coordinate is a measurement. The family titles attribute the schedule-adequate case to products and the feedback case to the other six datasets, matching panel c, so they are compared with titles the generator derives from the measured outcomes. Panel c is numerical: for the seven datasets in printed order, the two-line row label, the legend category of the marker colour, the paired effect versus q_C (five printed decimals) and its 95% test-stage interval (four printed decimals) from main Table 1; ogbn-products is the exact comparator identity, effect 0 without an interval (null). The plotted points and interval ends, measured on the 600-dpi rendering, agree with Table 1 at the rendering resolution. The panel title cites Table 2, whose effect column prints the same point effects; the intervals come from Table 1, which the caption cites. Peptides keeps the evaluated radius-arm values of Table 1; this contract does not assert that the arm passed the registered confirmation gate. Zero lines compare at six decimals. No target was taken from a generator output.

supplementary_figure_S6_cost_model_trunc.evidence_kind: analytical Note S19 cost-model coordinates at declared dataset statistics, evaluated at the observed per-member multipliers of Table S23
supplementary_figure_S6_cost_model_trunc.note: Every printed element is enumerated. Panel a: the six 50%-resolvent-step multiplier curves at the domain start T = 1, the registered T = 8 and the domain end T = 64, the six dotted measured multipliers and the 50% annotation. Panel b: all twelve admissible-order bars (six admitted datasets at 25% and 50% resolvent steps), their twelve printed labels, both share levels and the registered T = 8 line. Panel c: all fifteen printed ogbn-proteins markers T = 2..16, their domain, the registered T = 8 line, the printed bound label f_res <= 0.063, the title multiplier m = 1.20, the dataset and the caption's reduced sensor (k = 32, P_s = 4), compared with the registered proteins configuration. The sensing share s = 0.06 is shared by all panels; it is the declared residual share of that sensor and is not derived from (k, P_s) here (Note S19's s_sense = 8 r (k/d)/P_s would give 0.073 for it). Coordinates are independent evaluations of the Note S19 identities (formulas) at the source inputs; they are not copied from a display build. The printed labels and Note S19's admitted orders require the unrounded r = E/(N d): the three-decimal r of Note S19 and Table S6c would give 37 and 19 for arxiv instead of the printed 36 and 18, so the rounded r is a comparison of Table S6c only, never an input here. The bar labels are the nearest integer of the real bound, whereas Note S19 quotes integer parts of the admitted orders and one decimal below 2 (COCO at 50%: 14.84 is printed 15 in the figure and 'T <= 14' in Note S19; proteins at 50%: 1.88 is printed 2 in the figure and 'T <= 1.9' in Note S19). A bound above the axis is drawn at T = 64 and labelled >64; the Roman-empire bounds (309.0 at 25% and 155.0 at 50% with these statistics) are not displayed and are not targets. In the printed panel b the two rotated labels of each pair sit at their own bar's height but are horizontally interchanged; the label-to-bar association follows the label heights and agrees with the formula. Panel c's 0.063 is the analytical model bound at the registered order; the executed resolvent fraction (f_res column of Table S6c, 0.061 on proteins) and the executed sensor settings are observations that the figure does not plot and are not targets. The vector geometry of the printed panels agrees with these coordinates (curves within about 1e-4 decade, markers within 1e-4, bars drawn at the bounds rounded to 0.1); it served only as a cross-check. Axis tick labels (1, 3.16 and 10 on panel a's logarithmic axis) and axis ranges are presentation, not targets. ogbn-products is not drawn: it returns q_C and has no deployed multiplier.

supplementary_figure_S7_acquisition_gate.evidence_kind: analytical certificate illustration and explicit log-normal gap model at the printed Table S21 quantiles
supplementary_figure_S7_acquisition_gate.note: Panel a, the conditional-region illustration of Proposition 9, is enumerated as the boundary m_ℓ/L_J = 2 r_ℓ (slope 2 through the origin) on the printed radius domain [0, 1] with its end values 0 and 2, both axis quantities, and the two region labels with their side of the boundary (retain above, acquire below); the 2.2 top of the plotted window is a presentation limit, not a target. Panel b is enumerated for each of the six admitted datasets as the legend median and 5th-percentile gaps (Table S21, in mnats), the legend text, the fitted log-normal parameters mu = ln(median) and sigma = (ln median - ln p5)/z_0.95, and the plotted density at the median (the peak) and at the threshold; shared targets are z_0.95, the registered threshold tau = 0.002 nats (Table S32) = 2 mnats with its label, the printed gap domain and both axis quantities. The density is an explicit model per unit natural-log gap ('density per log-gap'): g(x) = exp(-(ln x - mu)^2/(2 sigma^2))/(sigma sqrt(2 pi)), whose peak 1/(sigma sqrt(2 pi)) lies at the median and which does not depend on the gap unit; it is not a recovered empirical histogram, and no empirical gap distribution is a target. The domain 0.05-50 mnats is the printed extent of every curve (both ends lie on the 5e-2 and 5e1 minor ticks of the labelled logarithmic axis, whose limits are the default 5% logarithmic margins around exactly this range); the renderer's sampling inside it is not a target. Table S34's skip and retained fractions are not plotted and are not targets. The rendered raster agrees with the model at the printed quantiles (peak heights of the separable curves within 0.0003, boundary slope 2.00, threshold at 2.0 mnats); it served only as a cross-check.

supplementary_figure_S15_spectral_finger.evidence_kind: exact registered-action functions (panels a-c) with a measured oracle confidence bound and measured deployed effects (panel d)
supplementary_figure_S15_spectral_finger.note: Every panel is enumerated from the visible page-35 rendering and caption (the PDF text layer also carries a second, overlaid caption text that does not appear in the rendering; it is not used). Panel a: the eight transport-action curves A0-A7 (A8/A9 are hybrid resets without a spectral response), the printed domain [0, 2], T = 8, every curve at the seven edges of the uniform six-band partition that panel b names (g_a(0) = 1; g_a(1) equals the panel-c identity coefficient), every zero crossing in [0, 2] (none for A6 and A7: null) and the zero reference line. The function is g_a(lambda) = sum_t c_t (1 - lambda)^t for T_a = (1 - nu) I + nu[(1 - rho) P + rho K~], with K~_{eta,T} = eta sum_{t=0..T} (1 - eta)^t P^t + (1 - eta)^{T+1} I (main Eq. 9) for resolvent actions and K~ = P for the nominal and one-step modes, P = I - L_sym in the symmetric frame. Coordinates were evaluated in exact rational arithmetic from the Table S6 constants and are compared at six decimals as deterministic model coordinates; the 401-point plotting grid is renderer sampling and is not a target. Panel b: all 42 printed two-decimal cells, the reference action A0 and the exact band edges (the tick labels print them to two decimals). An independent exact maximization of |g_a - g_A0| on each band reproduces every printed cell within half a unit; the closest case is A7 on [1, 4/3], exact maximum 0.375006, printed 0.38. Panel c: executed range nu[(1 - rho) + rho sum_t t eta (1 - eta)^t] and identity coefficient (1 - nu) + nu rho[eta + (1 - eta)^{T+1}] (nu and 1 - nu for one-step actions) at six decimals, their printed bar and 'id' labels at two decimals, the maximum-reach squares and the dotted nominal level 0.70. Panel d: the white bar is |U(Delta_oracle)| of Table S4, an upper confidence limit, so the headroom denominator is the oracle confidence bound and not its point estimate; the realized part is |Delta(q_D)|, the deployed rule's paired test effect of Table 1 (zero for products, where q_C is returned), the same point estimate of |Delta_sel(q_D)| that Figure S17b divides by this bound; the blue bar is |U(Delta_oracle)| - |Delta(q_D)|, the lower bound on headroom the deployed rule leaves unrealized. The four-decimal S4 bound fixes the white bar to 0.05 mnats and the five-decimal Table 1 effect fixes the realized part to 0.005 mnats, so their difference can deviate by 0.055 mnats, more than half a unit at one decimal: blue bars are compared at whole mnats (products, with no effect term, at one decimal) while both components keep their printed precision. The rendered bar heights agree with these definitions on visual inspection; no coordinate was read from the image or from a generator output. Panels a-c are protocol identities; panel d still requires the original oracle search and test evaluations.

main_figure_5_deployment_economics.evidence_kind: measured scores, costs and effects with Definition 2 curves and S23b timing anchors
main_figure_5_deployment_economics.note: All four panels are enumerated from the page-12 rendering, caption and legends. (a) For each of the seven datasets: the full-depth plant cost (E nominal executions, the cost unit of Table 2 and S15b) and score that normalize both axes; q_C at C_qC/C_plant; the deployed rule at its expected cost with the tick at its assurance cost (Table S23); both retrained architectures of S15 at their declared per-member cost-range endpoints (S15 lines 155-159, as the caption states); every score in points (AP x 100 for Peptides, with S26's four-decimal AP for Peptides' q_C and deployed rule); the three legend roles. For products the deployed rule is q_C itself (Tables 1-2: q_C returned; C_expected = C_assure = C_qC); the printed filled marker sits on the q_C diamond, so its coordinates equal q_C's. (b) The six deployed rules in printed order: lambda*, the range from the 95% interval of Delta and the points-per-unit rate of each label (Table 2, repeated by the annotations). (c) The six expected-cost lines and the two dashed assurance-cost lines (arxiv, Pascal) of U = |Delta| - lambda dEC on the printed domain lambda in [0, 10]: value at both domain ends, slope (added work) and zero crossing (Table 2's lambda* for the expected lines; |Delta|/C_ctrl for the assurance lines, because C_assure - C_qC = C_ctrl by the S23 definition), and the zero line; the dashed lines leave the printed y-window before lambda = 10, so their domain-end values check the function rather than a visible point. (d) theta = 0.1, the printed domain t_nom in [1e-4, 1e2] s, the six curves M* = 3600 C_qual/[theta (E C(q_D) - C(q_C)) t_nom] (their M* t_nom constant from Tables 2/S23b and log10 M* at both domain ends from S41 C_qual and S23 costs), and each S23b operating point: t_nom, the thick segment drawn on its curve over S23b's t_nom range (endpoints confirmed against the rendered axis; t range and log10 M* at its ends, ascending M*), and the printed label (mantissa, exponent and the shared Pascal, COCO label). Marker shapes (squares for Pascal and COCO) are presentation. Renderer sampling (101 prices, 61 times) is not a target. Roles: S23b's t_nom is the anchor-derived nominal time (geometric mean of the throughput and training-time anchors for arxiv, proteins and Roman; the launch-bound training-time anchor for Pascal and Peptides; COCO shares Pascal's anchor) and the brackets are those adopted anchors, not executed timing; a newly executed nominal_time measurement is compared with them as a separate quantity. Precision covers the propagated rounding of the printed inputs: relative costs to three decimals; score gains to one decimal, except whole points for COCO (plant printed 31.6) and Peptides (plant printed 0.704 AP, retrained 0.714/0.713), whose scores are compared at their printed precision; panel c intercepts, expected-cost slopes and crossings to two decimals, assurance slopes (C_ctrl) to three and domain-end values to one; log10 M* to two decimals, one at the low-t end of the Roman, Pascal, COCO and Peptides brackets. Table 2's range ends are compared as printed: Peptides' 6.5 needs an unrounded Table 1 lower endpoint at or below about -0.004715 (at dEC = 0.731), since the printed -0.0047 alone gives 6.43; no endpoint is inferred from it. Consistency was verified independently: Definition 2 at the printed inputs reproduces every Table 2 lambda* and M* t_nom and every S23b M* label within the inputs' printed precision. Main Figure 5's declared inputs do not include the timing_anchors record set; its generator reads that set when supplied, and the bracket targets otherwise remain missing comparisons.
